text:
marta-cs: FYI - Escalation from ACME (CS-4928). They reported an increase in hallucinations and broken table formatting after our quantization rollout yesterday. They say code examples now return truncated code blocks and numeric columns are shuffled. Attachments: sample prompt/response and request IDs. They believe it started around the INT8 profile flip on the eu dedicated pool. :sos:

eli-support: Thanks for the heads up. Customer included a request_id 02d3b7f6 and model variant 'gptx-13b-int8-v2'. They also pasted the failing prompt + output (see below). Billing/auth unaffected, this is clearly a quality regression.

marta-cs: Sample (from customer):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED-KEY>
{
  "model":"gptx-13b-int8-v2",
  "input":"Generate a markdown table summarizing the payroll: name, salary, tax_pct.
Employees:
- Alice, 120000, 30%
- Bob, 90000, 25%
- Cara, 110000, 28%"
}
```
Customer expected a 3-row table; got a single paragraph with hallucinated salaries and the 'tax_pct' column missing. They also attached request log: request_id=02d3b7f6, routed to pool dedicated-eu-1, host=ded-eu-01.

tony-eng: Ack. Can we get the exact server-side variant hash + model build id? Also need the quantization profile name used in the rollout (int8 profile name). Any quick diffs in the deployment manifest?

kai-ml: My suspicion: calibration dataset / clip scaling changed between int8_v1 -> int8_v2; small shift in zero-point or scale can significantly change logits for low-temperature deterministic outputs (tables, numbers). If FP8 experiments were packed into same pipeline, rounding behavior could differ. We should compare logprobs for a canonical prompt before/after and compute KL divergence.

eli-support: From the rollout notes: quant_profile: "int8_xp_v2" flipped at 2024-04-27T03:12:00Z for dedicated-eu-1, canary 10% -> 100% in 40m. Canary id: canary-20240427-62. Deploy bot logs:
```
deploy-bot: canary canary-20240427-62 promoted to 100% on dedicated-eu-1 at 2024-04-27T03:52:14Z
```

tony-eng: Ok, triage plan: 1) Reproduce locally with same model binary and quant_profile. 2) Run a small eval suite comparing outputs (exact text) and logprob deltas. 3) If regression confirmed, pin ACME to previous variant or revert quant_profile on that pool. 4) Create a perf/regression alert to block future auto-promotes.

marta-cs: Customer provided reproducible curl. Repro steps they used (copied):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${KEY}" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b-int8-v2","input":"<their prompt>","temperature":0.0}'
```
They ran it 5x and saw deterministic but incorrect table output each time.

kai-ml: Repro commands for internal eval (use this to get logits and compare):
```
# fetch model binaries for both variants
python infra/get_model.py --model gptx-13b --variant int8_v1 --out /tmp/m1
python infra/get_model.py --model gptx-13b --variant int8_v2 --out /tmp/m2
# run batch eval and dump token-level logprobs
python eval/harness.py --model-bin /tmp/m1 --prompt-file tests/payroll_prompts.txt --dump-logprobs /tmp/m1_probs.json
python eval/harness.py --model-bin /tmp/m2 --prompt-file tests/payroll_prompts.txt --dump-logprobs /tmp/m2_probs.json
# compare KL / token flips
python eval/compare_probs.py --a /tmp/m1_probs.json --b /tmp/m2_probs.json --metrics kl,flip_rate
```
Expectations: if KL > 0.1 and flip_rate > 5% on deterministic prompts, it's a strong regression.

tony-eng: Quick mitigation: pin ACME to known-good variant 'gptx-13b-fp16-v3' and set routing policy to prefer fp16 for table-like workloads. Steps: create route override for their org id and redeploy route. Command: `redwood routes set --org acme --model gptx-13b-fp16-v3 --priority 1000`. Also create a temporary canary rollback: `deploy-bot rollback canary-20240427-62 --pools dedicated-eu-1`. I can run the rollback if ops agrees. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: received rollback request for canary-20240427-62. ETA to execute after approvals: ~15m.

marta-cs: Customer asked for ETA. I'll tell them we can pin them within 30m and engineer will follow up with root cause once we confirm. Assigned to tony-eng and kai-ml.

kai-ml: If you want a fast root cause check: compare layerwise activation distributions between int8_v1 and int8_v2 on the payroll prompt. Clamping or per-channel scale changes will show up as mean/variance shifts in early transformer layers. Also check embedding-table quantization: if embedding table scales differ, tokenization -> embedding mismap can reorder numeric outputs.

eli-support: Note: We should also check if FP8 experiments were toggled in the same release; mixing INT8/FP8 conversion paths can introduce non-deterministic numeric behavior.

tony-eng: I'll start the rollback and run the eval harness. If rollback is successful, we issue a hotfix to block int8_xp_v2 auto-promote until calibration is re-run. Also will open an internal postmortem ticket with steps to improve our quantization rollout checks (add table/structured-output test cases to canary suite).

marta-cs: Customer updated the ticket: very appreciative of the quick action, wants confirmation when pinned. I'll update them after rollback completes. :pray:

eli-support: ticket CS-4928 updated: priority P1 -> assigned to engineering.

tony-eng: Update: rollback executed at 1719587620, canary reverted to int8_v1 on dedicated-eu-1. Running eval now.

marta-cs: Marking this thread as in-progress — will post back with ACME confirmation.

(Next steps pending: kai-ml to run activation diffs + re-calibrate quant_profile, tony to document rollback and add structured-output tests to canary. Oncall loop-in if regression repeats.)
